notes.summary: Draft base-K wide-polyannulus Picard proof using staged disc/circle gluing; no arbitrary-extension or full E1 claim.
notes.detailedSummary: Over K=C((s)), with |s|=exp(-1/8), Gruson's pure disc/circle SK0 theorem and determinant cancellation give the induction base. Filling one annular hole along its inner circle reduces the number of wide factors in both the boundary and filled spaces. Under the explicitly cited coherent-affinoid foundations, this proves Pic(P_m,K)=0 for every m. Gruson is never applied to a wide-annulus base.
notes.text:
Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8). This is an unverified proof draft under the named published analytic foundations. We prove Pic(P_m,K)=0 for every integer m>=1, where P_m,K is the product of the annuli |s|^m<=|z_j|<=|s|^(-m). More generally, the same proof covers finite products of closed discs, circles and closed annuli with positive radii in |K*|. No arbitrary-extension quantifier is claimed.

The precise external input is Gruson, Fibres vectoriels sur un polydisque ultrametrique, Ann. Sci. ENS (4) 1 (1968), 45–89, IV.5 Theorem 1. For a complete real-valued field, its H is a completed tensor product of disc algebras T_(1,r), r in Q tensor v(K*), and unit-circle algebras C. Its conclusion includes SK^0(H)=0, where SK^0 is coker(Z->K^0(H)), with 1 mapping to [H]. The entire statement, immediate proof and applied K0 dependencies were freshly read. This theorem is applied only to pure disc/circle products, never to a wide-annulus factor.

First SK^0(H)=0 implies Pic(H)=0. By the coherent-affinoid correspondence, a line bundle corresponds to a rank-one finite projective module P. Its K0 class is n[H]; rank gives n=1. Equality in the Grothendieck group of finite projectives gives P direct-sum Q isomorphic to H direct-sum Q for some finite projective Q. Taking determinants and tensoring by det(Q)'s inverse gives P isomorphic to H. Thus no vector-bundle cancellation theorem is needed. Radii in |K*| can be rescaled to unit discs and circles.

The coherent-affinoid correspondence and finite rational-cover descent are the Tate–Kiehl foundations, in Van der Put, Rigid analytic spaces (1975–76), 2.14–2.16.3 and 3.4.5–6. The complete printed immediate descent proof was read; it cites Kiehl for the deeper affinoid theorem. These are analytic G-covers for sheaves, not ordinary open covers for psh approximation.

Induct on the number k of wide-annulus factors, allowing any number of disc/circle factors. Write Z=A(r,R) times Y, where 0<r<R belong to |K*|. Assume the assertion for fewer than k wide factors. Both D(R) times Y and C(r) times Y have k-1 wide factors. Given ANY line bundle L on Z, its restriction to C(r) times Y is trivial by induction. Choose a frame there and identify it with the trivial bundle on D(r) times Y. The rational domains A(r,R) times Y and D(r) times Y cover D(R) times Y and intersect in C(r) times Y. With |a|=r their inequalities are |a/z|<=1 and |z/a|<=1; a and z generate the unit ideal. They form a finite admissible affinoid cover. Coherent descent glues an invertible sheaf L' on D(R) times Y. By induction L' is trivial, hence so is L. This proves the induction.

Explicitly in two variables, first fill the second hole of C_1 times A_2, using C_1 times C_2 and C_1 times D_2, both pure products. Then extend L on A_1 times A_2 to D_1 times A_2 along C_1 times A_2. Finally fill the second hole using D_1 times C_2 and D_1 times D_2. The intermediate wide product is proved by filling, rather than by applying an arbitrary-base restricted-variable theorem.

Taking r=|s|^m and R=|s|^(-m) proves the needed F_K for every m. No formal-model extension, topological contractibility, pro-homotopy substitution or broader factoriality claim is used. This closes a finite base-field foundation; it does not solve P16.7.

Full proof artifacts: notes/n1.md, P16.7-standalone-paper.tex and proof-companion.md. Exact source units and reading distinctions are in source-application-ledger.md and sources-LOCALONLY/. Rerun the own finite diagnostic with `python scripts/diagnostics.py`; it illustrates finite gluing states and does not prove analytic descent.

notes.summary: Draft base-field nonalgebraization of the explicit proper analytic surface, excluding every separated finite-type algebraic-space algebraization.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1, compatible infinite frames trivialize torus line bundles. Inner Gauss estimates, the signed Laurent recurrence and intrinsic pole ideals yield Gamma(X,M)=K for periods (s^8,2),(3,s^8). Smoothness reflection, generic-field hypotheses and analytification of descended divisor data exclude all separated finite-type K-algebraic spaces. Deeper analytic foundations remain explicitly cited; no arbitrary-extension or full equation theorem is claimed.
notes.text:
Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8. Put T=(G_m^2)^an, lambda_1=(t,2), lambda_2=(3,t), Lambda=<lambda_1,lambda_2>, and X=T/Lambda. With n1, the argument below no longer assumes F_K. It is an unverified proof draft under the explicitly cited analytic foundations and excludes every separated finite-type K-algebraic-space algebraization, not only projective schemes or group algebraizations.

Write x=(-log|z_1|,-log|z_2|). Translation by lambda(n) changes x by n. Inverse images of rectangles of widths less than one have disjoint nonidentity translates and give ordinary open quotient charts. Their analytic transitions are locally constant deck translations satisfying the cocycle. Conrad–Temkin, Non-archimedean analytification of algebraic spaces, author version dated 24 February 2009, Lemma 4.2.3, supplies the applied open-gluing statement. Its full immediate proof was freshly read. The action relation in T times_K T is a locally finite union of closed translation graphs: compact tropical-coordinate ranges bound the possible integer differences. Its map is a closed immersion. Lemma 4.2.4 and the adjacent full closed-immersion descent proof justify the quotient's closed diagonal. Thus X is analytically separated.

The strict compact polyannulus x^(-1)([0,1]^2) surjects onto X. A center in (1/8 Z)^2 within 1/16 of a lifted point gives a closed rectangle of width 1/2 inside an open quotient chart of width 3/4. Its inverse image is a strict affinoid neighborhood. Hence X is good and strict. Ordinary torus charts show smoothness, pure dimension two and empty relative boundary. Compactness, separatedness and empty boundary give properness. Integral Laurent polyannuli form a nested connected exhaustion of T, so X is connected. Only base-K geometry is asserted.

We prove Pic(T)=0 with compatibility, not unrelated finite frames. Put a=1/8 and P_m={|s|^m<=|z_i|<=|s|^(-m)}. By n1 a given line bundle has a frame e_m on each P_m. For a unit f=sum b_beta z^beta on P_m, its Gauss log norm on log-radii y in [-ma,ma]^2 is max(log|b_beta|+beta dot y). This and the norm of f^(-1) are convex and sum to zero, hence affine. A term attaining the maximum at an interior point agrees with that affine function: their nonnegative affine difference has an interior zero. Its slope is an integral alpha. Vertex inequalities give

|b_beta/b_alpha| exp(ma |beta-alpha|_1)<=1.

Thus f=b_alpha z^alpha(1+g), with zero constant coefficient in g and ||g||_(P_j)<=|s|^(m-j) for j<m. No boundary smallness on P_m is claimed. On all R^2 the same argument forces every global torus unit to be exactly b z^alpha; another exponent would dominate along a ray.

Normalize successive frames by global scalar monomials so e_(m+1)|P_m=(1+g_m)e_m. For fixed j the product p_j=product_(m=j)^infinity(1+g_m)|P_j converges to a unit: its first factor is a unit, and later errors tend to zero, with inverse tails converging geometrically. E_j=e_j p_j satisfies E_(j+1)|P_j=E_j. Since P_j lies in the interior of P_(j+1), this admissible exhaustion glues the frames globally. Therefore Pic(T)=0.

Pull a line bundle on X to T and choose a global frame. A section becomes an analytic Laurent function f with

f(lambda z)=c_lambda z^(h_lambda) f(z).

Multipliers are global units, hence scalar monomials. Commuting deck transformations gives lambda_1^(h_2)=lambda_2^(h_1). If h_1=(A,B), h_2=(C,D), this reads t^C 2^D=3^A t^B. Valuations give C=B, and rational prime factorization gives A=D=0. Thus h_1=(0,k), h_2=(k,0).

For k!=0 choose n=(1,sign k), lambda=lambda(n), h=(k n_2,k n_1). Then h!=0 and Q=v(lambda^h)=2|k|>0. From a nonzero Laurent coefficient a_m, comparison gives

a_(m+jh)=a_m c^j lambda^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2), j>=0.

Its valuation has leading term -Qj(j+1)/2 and tends to minus infinity. This contradicts coefficient decay on the fixed unit polyannulus as exponents escape. For k=0, two nonzero exponents m,m' would satisfy lambda_i^(m-m')=1 for both periods; their valuations force m=m'. Hence a nonzero section is a single scalar monomial and has no zeros.

This treats all meromorphic functions using their pole ideals. Smooth affinoid algebras are noetherian regular. The precise commutative-algebra inputs, freshly read with complete immediate proofs, are Stacks 0AG0: every regular local ring is a UFD; and 031T: a noetherian normal domain equals the intersection of its height-one localizations inside its fraction field. On a fraction chart F=g/h, define J={b in O:bF in O}, the kernel of multiplication by g to O/(h). It is coherent. Local UFD cancellation makes it principal at each prime, with exactly the pole orders, hence finite locally free of rank one. Its intrinsic definition glues these ideals on overlaps, giving O(-P)=J for the effective Cartier pole divisor. Affinoid coherence and analytic descent are the named Tate–Kiehl foundations.

Trivialize J on T using Pic(T)=0. Its inclusion in O gives an analytic f_0 with divisor P. Because f_0 is a section of J, f_1=F f_0 is analytic by J's definition; this does not assume an arbitrary meromorphic sheaf section is already one global affinoid fraction. The normal intersection theorem checks the same fact on local fraction charts. At a pole f_1 has order zero, and elsewhere f_0 has order zero, so there is no common height-one divisor. Lambda-invariance of F identifies the translated J with J; the two global frames differ by an analytic unit. Thus f_0 and f_1 have the same scalar-monomial multipliers. The recurrence forces both to be scalar multiples of the same monomial. Therefore Gamma(X,M)=K. Every meromorphic pole divisor is included.

Suppose a separated finite-type K-algebraic space Y has Y^an isomorphic to X. Conrad–Temkin 2.3.1 reflects smoothness, and Example 2.3.2 compares closed-point residue fields and completed local rings; their complete statements and immediate proofs were freshly read. The strict good separated Berkovich/rigid dictionary applies. Thus Y is smooth of dimension two. A clopen algebraic decomposition would analytify to one; each nonempty finite-type piece has a closed point and nonempty analytification. Y is connected. Its finitely many regular irreducible components are disjoint and open, so Y is integral.

All Stacks 0ENA hypotheses are checked: regular noetherian etale charts have only codimension-zero weakly associated points; noetherian finite-type charts satisfy 0BB1's finite-component conditions; separatedness gives decency, and the generic point has a field monomorphism. Stacks 086U gives a dense open scheme locus, containing the unique generic point of integral Y. Current 0ENA, 0EN6 and 0END, freshly read with their full immediate proofs, identify local total fractions and the global rational field K(Y). A dense affine scheme open and Noether normalization give transcendence degree two over K.

Analytic passage is separate. A rational function on regular Y has a Cartier pole divisor, invertible sheaf and numerator/denominator regular sections descending algebraically through etale charts. Conrad–Temkin's exact coherent analytification functor, defined by etale descent and compatible with pullback, analytifies them. Its applied passages and immediate descent proofs were freshly read. Ducros, Families of Berkovich spaces, 2.1.3–4, states regularity of the algebraic-to-analytic local-ring map for a scheme locally finite type over a k-affinoid algebra. It cites Berkovich 1993 Proposition 2.6.2 for flatness and Ducros 2009 Theorem 3.3 for regularity; these remain honestly cited deeper foundations, not fabricated immediate proofs. Our base K is affinoid. The local flat map is faithfully flat and preserves nonzerodivisors, so the descended sections' ratio is analytic meromorphic, with this property descending across analytic etale charts. A fraction equalizer alone is not a general analytic meromorphic sheaf theorem.

Injection is checked by choosing a closed point of a dense affine scheme open outside the zeros of a nonzero numerator and denominator. Its finite residue extension is complete and supplies an analytic point where the fraction is nonzero. Thus K(Y) embeds into Gamma(X,M)=K while fixing K, contradicting transcendence degree two.

This excludes ALL separated finite-type K-algebraic spaces. No arbitrary-extension conclusion is claimed. The explicit real analytic datum is theta=d'd''(|x|^2/2), whose deck changes are smooth Hessian-null affine functions. No ample algebraic line bundle is introduced. The full intrinsic unbounded finite-energy equation remains unproved.

notes.summary: New constant-energy bounded branch pencils disprove uniform energy-bounded compactness and impose a necessary finite-dual branch-tail bound.
notes.detailedSummary: For every real N>=1 the ordinary bounded class C_theta contains U_N with a genuine mass-one off-section atom and E(U_N)=-1/6-N/3. The pencil V_(a,N)=u0+aD_N has MA=(1-a²)MA(u0)+a²MA(U_N) and E=-1/6-a³N/3. Taking a=N^(-1/3) gives normalized energy -2/3 and rigid value -1/4-N^(2/3), ruling out uniform compactness on that energy-bounded family. Finite bounded dual energy forces a branch-mass bound of order N^(-2/3). Weaker compactness, a sufficient criterion and unbounded E1 remain open.
notes.text:
Use the base-K quotient of n2. This note independently constructs the bounded ordinary-local operator, verifies the checkpoint for EVERY real N>=1 and proves the new constant-energy and measure-tail consequences. These are unverified mathematical drafts under the named analytic foundations, not a counterexample to the original P16.7 equation.

Write DD=d'd'', x_j=-log|z_j|, q=|x|^2/2 and theta=DDq on a deck sheet. Its change under x->x+n is n dot x+|n|^2/2, smooth and DD-null. Define C_theta as the continuous real functions u such that q+u is locally on ORDINARY opens a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD smooth functions with middle-positive Hessian. This explicit generated bounded class is not identified with a larger psh theory.

The coefficient-space correction is essential. In an m-dimensional moment presentation, symmetric (p,p) coefficients are symmetric matrices on Lambda^p R^m, with the exterior sign; their dimension is d(d+1)/2, d=binomial(m,p). Middle positivity is PSD. For m=4,p=2, d=6 and the coefficient dimension is 21. Strong squares ww^t satisfy Q(w)=w12 w34-w13 w24+w14 w23=0 and span EXACTLY 20 dimensions. Indeed Q=0 characterizes decomposable bivectors, by rank two of their skew matrices. Put x=(w12,w13,w14), y=(w34,-w24,w23), so Q=x dot y. A quadratic form vanishing on Q=0 has no pure-x or pure-y part, and its remaining part x^t B y vanishes whenever y is perpendicular to x. Hence B^t x is proportional to every x; testing basis vectors and their pairwise sums makes B scalar. The annihilator is exactly the one-dimensional span of Q. The witness e12+e34 has Q=1. Thus the strong cone is NOT an ambient order-unit cone.

For the middle cone, a Euclidean positive form lambda has lambda^p represented by p! I. On compact tropical support every symmetric smooth coefficient matrix B satisfies -C lambda^p<=B<=C lambda^p. A nonnegative cutoff equal to one on that support decomposes a test into two middle-positive compact tests inside the SAME ordinary open. Finite moment-chart localization globalizes this. CLD-v2 1.2.6–13 and 6.5.1–3 give these precise middle-cone/decomposition inputs; 15.1.1 and 15.2.3–9 supply ordinary moments, cutoffs and density. Their full applied statements and immediate proofs were freshly read. The good separated boundaryless X meets their local-separation hypotheses. No strong domination from 7.2.9 is used.

For a symmetric middle-positive current T and positive test eta, phi-><T,phi eta> is a positive scalar functional. A cutoff plateau bounds it by the compact supremum norm. Smooth scalar density and Riesz give a Radon measure. Decompose beta=eta_+-eta_- and subtract their coefficient measures; equality on smooth scalars proves independence and support in supp(beta). Antisymmetric tests pair to zero. Continuous multiplication is defined and satisfies

|<bT,beta>|<=sup_K|b| <T,eta_++eta_->,

where K is their compact support union. If positive T_j->T weakly and b_j->b locally uniformly, approximate b on K by a smooth g within epsilon and split b_jT_j-bT=(b_j-g)T_j+g(T_j-T)+(g-b)T. The first/last terms obey the bound with bounded positive-current masses, the middle tends to zero; then let epsilon vanish. This reconstructs CLD-v2 7.2.8 and 7.2.11–12 using the corrected middle order unit.

For closed symmetric T and smooth h, complementary-degree Leibniz gives DD(hT)=DDh wedge T. Arbitrary continuous multiplication is not claimed to preserve closedness. For u,v in C_theta, set alpha_u=theta+DD[u] and locally, f=q+u,g=q+v,

B(u,v)=DD(f DD[g]).

Smooth-positive approximants give DDg_j->DDg and f_j DDg_j->f DDg by the preceding lemma. Differentiating proves convergence of their positive symmetric smooth mixed products, independently of approximation. Smooth DD-null changes glue the products on ordinary overlaps. Differences inherit bilinearity by subtraction. The applied bounded recursive units are CLD-v2 8.5.1/3/5, 8.7.1–4 and 8.8.1, 8.8.4–8. No arbitrary-current density, upward recognition or 8.6.7 continuous-multiplier closedness is used.

Canonical integration in CLD-v2 14.3.1–5 and 14.5.2–3 retains actual generic Artinian lengths and calibration degrees. The full immediate proofs were read; their deeper Berkovich/calibration foundations remain cited. CLD-v2 15.7.1–2 gives canonical tropical level equal to pure analytic dimension, with the analytic boundary, on a topologically separated space. Thus the positive top current is an actual analytic Radon measure. Our identity and translated identity moments have saturated Z^2 lattice and actual degree one. The exterior factor is 2!, so theta^2=2 i_*dx for probability Haar dx. RAW mass is two.

Globally B(u,v)=theta wedge alpha_v+DD(u alpha_v), and theta wedge alpha_v=theta^2+DD(v theta). Pairing differentiated terms with 1 on compact boundaryless X makes them zero; hence each B has mass two. Define MA_theta(u)=B(u,u). The multiplication argument proves continuity under uniform convergence WITHIN C_theta. Dini handles decreasing limits only when still continuous and in that class. Smooth convex nondecreasing regularization proves convexity and finite-max stability. For w=max(u,v-epsilon), ordinary locality and equal mass give

MA_theta(v){u<v-epsilon}<=2-MA_theta(u){u>v-epsilon}=MA_theta(u){u<=v-epsilon}.

Let epsilon decrease to zero; both sets increase to {u<v}. This proves bounded comparison, not full-E1 comparison or uniqueness.

Let G(y)=y^2/2-y/2+1/12 on [0,1], extended periodically. Its mean is zero and G''=dy-delta_0. Put u0=-G(x1)-G(x2). Positive periodic convolution gives smooth-positive approximants, so

A=alpha_u0, A^2=2 delta_i(0),
theta wedge A=i_*(dy tensor delta_0+delta_0 tensor dy).

The range of u0 is [-1/6,1/12], and u0=-1/6 on the ENTIRE fibre F=tau^-1(0). On its ordinary sheet V={|x_j|<1/4}, for every real N>=1 put r=exp(-N), ell_j=log max(r,|z_j-1|), b_j=log max(1,|z_j|), d_j=ell_j-b_j and D_N=max(d1,d2). Real convex thresholds and Gauss seminorms permit arbitrary positive r; no strict-affinoid assertion for radius r is needed. Each d_j<=0 and is zero if |z_j|!=1. Thus D_N vanishes off F and extends continuously by zero outside V. Its negative locus W={|z1-1|<1,|z2-1|<1} is ORDINARY open, contained in F.

For U_N=u0+D_N, direct calculation gives on V

q+U_N=max(ell1+b2,b1+ell2)-(1/2)log|z1z2|-1/6.

Near a zero of z_j-1 the truncated ell_j is constant; omit that inactive coordinate. Elsewhere the involved analytic functions are invertible and their logarithms give ordinary moment charts. Sums/maxima are convex functions of these logarithms, while the last logarithm is pluriharmonic. Softmax or convolution gives actual ordinary smooth-positive approximants. No logarithmic chart crosses a zero. Consequently U_N belongs to the EXACT C_theta.

In W put w_j=z_j-1. Its weight is log max(r,|w1|,|w2|)-1/6. The bidisc Gauss point xi_N with both w-radii r is in W. There |z_j-1|=r<1, whereas the original Gauss point i(0) has value one; xi_N is off the original section. Near xi_N the w_j are invertible and form a translated identity moment with degree one and saturated lattice. In y_j=log|w_j|+N, regularize max(0,y1,y2) by epsilon log(1+exp(y1/epsilon)+exp(y2/epsilon)). Its gradient is a diffeomorphism onto the triangle p_j>0,p1+p2<1. Change of variables gives integral det(Hess)=1/2; rescaling gives concentration at zero. Multiplication by 2! gives mass one. CLD-v2 5.8.1–6 places the smooth measures on the actual translated Gauss section; continuity of that section, checked by seminorm evaluation as in 12.1.2–5, gives convergence against analytic continuous tests. Operator continuity identifies the atom. Away from the vertex the weight is locally affine or depends on one coordinate after affine subtraction; near a zero omit its inactive log. Its square therefore vanishes there. Hence MA_theta(U_N)|W=delta_xi_N, with total mass two. The other mass one outside W is NOT identified.

On W both q and u0 are constant, so theta|W=A|W=0. D_N is zero on the complement, including the boundary. Coefficient measures and ordinary locality give D_N theta=D_N A=0 globally, without nonsmooth integration by parts. Therefore theta wedge alpha_U_N=theta wedge A. Off F, U_N=u0 on ordinary neighborhoods, so MA_theta(U_N) is supported on F. D_N also vanishes on the original Gauss section. For

E_theta(u)=(1/3) integral u(theta^2+theta wedge alpha_u+MA_theta(u)),

the COMPLETE three integrals for U_N are 0, -1/6 and -1/3-N. Thus E_theta(U_N)=-1/6-N/3. At the rigid y=(1,1), U_N(y)=-1/6-N, giving E_theta(U_N)-2U_N(y)=1/6+5N/3. The mass-two rigid atom therefore has infinite C_theta dual energy. Its restricted separable dual is 1/6, as independently computed in n4. An extension inherits the infinity ONLY after verified containment of C_theta and identity of bounded energy.

The NEW energy-bounded test is V_(a,N)=u0+aD_N=(1-a)u0+aU_N, 0<=a<=1. Bilinearity for differences gives A wedge DD D_N=DD(D_N A)=0. Expansion yields

MA_theta(V_(a,N))=(1-a^2)MA_theta(u0)+a^2 MA_theta(U_N),
theta wedge alpha_V=theta wedge A.

Both right-hand measures are actual bounded measures supported on F. D_N vanishes at i(0) and integrates to -N against MA(U_N). The energy integrals are therefore 0, -1/6 and -1/3-a^3N. Hence

E_theta(V_(a,N))=-1/6-a^3N/3,
V_(a,N)(y)=-1/6-aN,
sup V_(a,N)=1/12.

The supremum follows from D_N<=0 and a maximum of u0 outside F. Along this entire admissible pencil, dE/da=-a^2N=integral D_N MA(V_(a,N)); this is pencil variation, not all-direction variation.

Choose a=N^(-1/3). Then E=-1/2, while V(y)=-1/6-N^(2/3). Subtracting the supremum gives sup v_N=0, E(v_N)=-2/3 and v_N(y)=-1/4-N^(2/3). A uniformly relatively compact family of continuous functions on compact X is uniformly bounded. Thus this normalized energy-bounded family is NOT uniformly relatively compact. Unlike the unscaled family, its energies are bounded. This disproves only uniform compactness in C_theta; weaker useful compactness, unbounded E1 membership and unbounded continuity remain open. All these potentials have the same skeleton restriction, so theta-reference skeleton L1 is not a separated topology even on this energy-bounded family.

There is also a NEW necessary measure condition. For positive Radon mu of RAW mass two assume M=E*_C_theta(mu)<infinity. Put J0=E_theta(u0)-integral u0 dmu and C=M-J0>=0. Let L_N=integral(-D_N)dmu. Testing V gives

aL_N-a^3N/3<=C for every a in [0,1].

For N>3C/2, L_N>N would contradict the a=1 inequality. Hence L_N<=N. If L_N>0, maximize at a=sqrt(L_N/N), obtaining (2/3)L_N^(3/2)/sqrt(N)<=C. Thus

L_N<=(3C/2)^(2/3)N^(1/3),
mu(B_N)<=(3C/2)^(2/3)N^(-2/3), for N>=1 and N>3C/2,
B_N={|z1-1|<=exp(-N),|z2-1|<=exp(-N)}.

The second inequality follows from -D_N=N on B_N. If C=0, the tests force L_N=0. The bidiscs decrease to y, so mu({y})=0. This is necessary, not sufficient, and supplies no existence theorem. It tests actual branch support missed by skeletal marginals.

notes.summary: Complete reconstructed circle equation/envelope theory, explicitly restricted to separable skeletal directions.
notes.detailedSummary: The periodic Green kernel parameterizes circle curvature probabilities and solves every skeletal product equation uniquely within S_theta. Circle compactness, energy identities, contact orthogonality and every circle-direction first variation are proved. Restricted dual energy is finite for every mass-two analytic measure and sees only marginals, so it cannot replace full admissibility. The all-direction unbounded E1 obligations remain unresolved.
notes.text:
Use X of n2 and the bounded operator of n3. Let C=R/Z with probability Lebesgue dy and H={h continuous: rho_h=dy+h''>=0 distributionally}. Testing against one gives mass one. The periodic G(y)=y^2/2-y/2+1/12 has mean zero and G''=dy-delta_0. For any circle probability nu, h_nu=-G*nu satisfies rho_h_nu=nu. Conversely h-h_rho_h has zero second derivative and is periodic, hence constant. Since G ranges in [-1/24,1/12] and is 1/2-Lipschitz, mean-zero potentials range in [-1/12,1/24], have Lipschitz constant 1/2 and oscillation at most 1/8. Sup-zero normalization gives a bounded equicontinuous closed family, uniformly compact by Arzela–Ascoli. Positivity passes by distributional testing. This is circle compactness only.

Define S_theta={h1(tau1)+h2(tau2):h_j in H}. Positive periodic convolution gives actual ordinary smooth-positive approximants, hence S_theta is contained in C_theta. Diagonal smooth Hessians and n3's continuity give the ANALYTIC equalities

B(h1+h2,k1+k2)=i_*(rho_h1 tensor rho_k2+rho_k1 tensor rho_h2),
MA_theta(h1+h2)=2 i_*(rho_h1 tensor rho_h2).

Product probabilities converge weakly first on product tests and then by Stone–Weierstrass on all continuous tests; continuity of the actual section gives analytic convergence. Every measure 2i_*(nu1 tensor nu2) has solution h_nu1+h_nu2. Marginals recover each nu_j, so uniqueness modulo constants holds WITHIN S_theta. X itself need not be a product of curves.

Every h is Lipschitz. Set e(h)=integral h dy-(1/2)integral|h'|^2dy. Periodic convolution gives uniform convergence of h, L2 convergence of derivatives and weak curvature convergence. Consequently

integral h d rho_h=integral h dy-integral|h'|^2dy,
e(k)-e(h)=integral(k-h)d rho_h-(1/2)integral|k'-h'|^2dy.

Thus e is concave, strictly concave modulo constants, with derivative on each admissible circle segment given by curvature integration. E_sep(h1+h2)=2(e(h1)+e(h2)) is independent of shifting constants between factors and satisfies E_sep(u+c)=E_sep(u)+2c. The three bounded analytic energy measures yield respectively 2 sum integral h_jdy, sum(integral h_jdy+integral h_jd rho_hj), and 2 sum integral h_jd rho_hj. Their average equals E_sep. No all-direction variation is assumed.

For ANY positive analytic Radon mu of RAW mass two, define E*_sep(mu)=sup_(u in S_theta)(E_sep(u)-integral u dmu). Normalize each factor by sup h_j=0. Then -1/4<=u<=0 and E_sep(u)<=0; u=0 gives 0<=E*_sep(mu)<=1/2. Let nu_j=(tau_j)_*mu/2. The objective is 2 sum(e(h_j)-integral h_jdnu_j), whose energy-difference identity gives maximizing curvature rho_hj=nu_j, uniquely modulo constants. The maximizing MA is the skeletal product of these marginals, regardless of mu's original support or correlations. Thus restricted finiteness is not the original criterion. For y=(1,1), its value at u0 is -1/6-2(-1/6)=1/6, although MA(u0)=2delta_i(0), not 2delta_y. The full bounded dual infinity is separately proved in n3.

All circle obstacle claims are also reconstructed. For continuous a let P(a)=sup{h in H:h<=a}. Constants below min a ensure nonemptiness. Common Lipschitz bounds, the obstacle upper bound and a constant lower bound make the supremum finite and continuous. On R, y^2/2+P(a)(y) is a supremum of convex functions, hence convex. Therefore P(a) belongs to H and is the largest admissible minorant. Monotonicity and constant translation give ||P(a)-P(b)||_infinity<=||a-b||_infinity.

Put p=P(a), F(y)=y^2/2+p(y). If curvature charged a noncontact arc, choose a short interval [c,d] compactly inside it with positive interior curvature and positive minimum clearance a-p. Replace F there by its endpoint chord. It raises F somewhere, while its slope lies between exterior one-sided slopes, preserving convexity. These slopes are bounded on the fixed compact arc, so the increase is bounded by a constant times d-c and can stay below the obstacle. Repeat on integer translates using F(y+n)=F(y)+ny+n^2/2; affine corrections preserve chords and periodicity of F-y^2/2. This contradicts maximality. Positive curvature on an arc can be localized in arbitrarily short such intervals. Thus rho_p is supported on {p=a} and integral(a-p)d rho_p=0.

For continuous v put p_b=P(a+bv). The energy-difference identity, its reverse and both contact statements give

b integral v d rho_pb<=e(p_b)-e(p)<=b integral v d rho_p.

Nonexpansiveness gives p_b->p uniformly. Distributional testing and fixed mass give rho_pb->rho_p weakly. Dividing by b, reversing inequalities for b<0, proves the derivative at zero of e(P(a+bv)) equals integral v d rho_p. Orthogonality and first variation therefore hold in EVERY circle direction, not for arbitrary analytic obstacles or a full intrinsic cone.

The full E1 attempt has concrete constraints: C_theta contains the branch pencils on the nonalgebraizable base-field example; its bounded products and mass are fixed. Defining a larger class merely by decreasing limits does not construct an operator outside the established continuous class. No inverse measure construction is substituted for MA.
